claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical dual-phase lamellar microstructure containing FCC/L12 and B2 phases.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and brittle failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries cause local stress concentrations and brittle failure in the untreated alloy.
A phase-selective or gradient annealing treatment can preferentially induce recovery and recrystallization near soft/hard lamellar interfaces.
The two phases of an annealed EHEA can respond differently, with recovery favored in B2 and recrystallization favored in the heavily deformed FCC/L12 phase.
Localized interfacial recovery or recrystallization will reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Annealing will enhance interfacial coherence and modify internal boundaries so that they present a lower barrier to dislocations.
The modified interfaces will improve dislocation transfer between the soft and hard phases.
Reducing dislocation accumulation will decrease local stress concentrations.
Lower interfacial stress concentrations will delay microcrack initiation and catastrophic damage during tensile straining.
The tailored annealing treatment will significantly increase room-temperature tensile elongation relative to the untreated alloy.
The tailored annealing treatment will maintain or slightly increase yield strength and ultimate tensile strength.
More uniform plastic deformation and reduced damage initiation will account for the retained or increased strength and improved ductility.
Annealing temperature and dwell time can be selected to modify the interfaces without coarsening the overall lamellar architecture.
Over-annealing could coarsen the microstructure or destroy the beneficial dual-phase architecture.
Insufficient annealing may fail to modify the interfaces adequately.
The proposed property improvement is intended to apply under standard room-temperature tensile testing conditions.
The quantitative increases in elongation and strength remain uncertain and require experimental validation.
